newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki ends down, sentiment clearly sours.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki ends down, sentiment clearly sours.

text.p: Shares closed almost 1.5 percent lower on Wednesday as livelier afternoon selling turned sentiment sour after a positive start, and investors remained wary of international bond markets, brokers said.

The HEX general index closed down 1.43 percent at 2,744.74 points after rising over two percent earlier to a 2,807.67-point session high, and the FOX portfolio and derivatives benchmark fell 1.5 percent to 956.24 points.

Orion strongly bucked the trend, with the B share up 8.00 markka at 199.00 after a massive 470,000 share in-house deal at 198.00 markka in both its B and A series at brokerage Evli, which declined to comment on the deal.

Brokers said a domestic owner had shown interest in switching a large chunk between Orion A and B and that international buyers were also probably involved in the transaction, and had made their presence felt.
"The race to get that deal has probably given a boost to the share," one broker said. Orion has recently been firm and last week presented a new Parkinson's drug in London.
Telecoms major Nokia fell 6.50 markka or 2.24 percent to 283.50 markka, its lowest since early January.
Forestries fell in line with Swedish forest industry stocks -- the index lost 2.22 percent with Enso and UPM-Kymmene down over 1.5 percent, and Enso's A share down almost five percent.

Interest rate jitters dragged Finland's largest banking group Merita to close 0.50 markka or 3.13 percent down at 15.50 markka -- its lowest since January 13 -- despite renewed speculation in other Nordic countries of finance sector consolidation, which has typically helped banks.
That talk was fuelled by news of the merger of Norwegian insurer Storebrand and Christiania Bank. However, it helped insurers, who posted modest gains against the trend.
